project_scope: Development of a deep-draft, all-weather container port as a satellite of Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, including construction of a 10,140 m offshore breakwater, reclamation, a 1,000 m contiguous berth per terminal (initial Phase 1), up to nine 1,000 m container terminals by 2040, associated quay infrastructure, road and rail connectivity, quarry sourcing of rock (≈32.1 million t for breakwater), and implementation of green and social mitigation measures.
project_constraints: Proximity to existing fishing harbour and fishermen settlements in the north
Shankodhar point in the middle of the sea must be preserved
Mangroves and rocky outcrop near the coast
Minimum 300 m clearance between shoreline and bund to avoid disturbing mangrove flow
Locating terminal and onshore facilities on reclaimed land
Minimize impact on adjoining population and villages
Rail and road access planned for minimal impact on adjoining village
Facilities for Coast Guard to improve security
Environmental considerations for green design concepts
Technical constraints due to site physical conditions
project_timeline: Phase 1 development targeting initial berth capacity and breakwater construction with reference capacity figures for 2030; Phase 2 expansion to achieve full master-plan capacity by 2040, including additional container terminals.
